verifications.claim: Gary Woodland underwent successful brain surgery in September 2023 to remove a benign lesion that was causing severe fear and anxiety symptoms.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Woodland had brain surgery in September 2023" (R1); "surgery in September of 2023 to remove a lesion on his brain... benign tumor... lesion was on the part of the brain that controls Woodland's fear and anxiety" (R2); "underwent brain surgery in Sept. 2023 to remove a brain lesion... pressing on the part of the brain that controlled fear and anxiety... confirm it was benign" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the timing, success, benign nature of the lesion/tumor, and its link to fear/anxiety symptoms.

verifications.claim: In May 2023, a lesion was discovered on Gary Woodland's brain.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Woodland first experienced symptoms in May 2023, then he underwent testing that revealed a brain lesion" (R3); "An MRI in May discovered the tumor" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state discovery via MRI/testing in May 2023.

verifications.claim: The lesion was pressing on the area responsible for controlling fear and anxiety.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The lesion was on the part of the brain that controls Woodland's fear and anxiety" (R2); "brain lesion pressing on the part of the brain that controlled fear and anxiety" (R3); "residual tumor sits near his amygdala, which controls emotions, in particular fear and anxiety" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements in sources link the lesion to the fear/anxiety control area.

verifications.claim: On Sept. 19, 2023, Gary Woodland underwent a craniotomy to remove the tumor.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "On Sept. 19, 2023, Woodland had brain surgery... drill a hole in his skull" (R2); "underwent a craniotomy on Sept. 19, 2023" (R3); "brain surgery... took place on September 18, 2023" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: R2 and R3 support Sept. 19 and craniotomy (drilling hole), but R8 contradicts with September 18.

verifications.claim: Doctors were able to remove a majority of the tumor.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "remove most of the lesion" (R2); "remove a majority of the tumor" (R3); "to remove much of the lesion" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state majority/most/much was removed.

verifications.claim: Some of the tumor was left to prevent potential loss of sight or motor function on Gary Woodland's left side.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "they had to leave some of it because otherwise Woodland would have had the possibility of losing sight in his left eye and the use of the left side of his body" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: R2 exactly matches the reason for leaving part of the tumor.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland returned to competition at the Sony Open in Hawaii in January 2024.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Woodland returned to competition in Jan. 2024 at the Sony Open in Hawaii" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on event, location, and date.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland revealed a PTSD diagnosis in March 2026 stemming from the ordeal.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "admitted that he’s been struggling with PTSD since his return... following brain surgery" (R1); "publicly admitted that he had PTSD... lingering effects from the lesion and the surgery" (R2); "opened up about... post-traumatic stress disorder" two weeks before Houston (late March 2026) (R4); "revealed a diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder... following surgery to remove a brain lesion in 2023" (R7); "In March 2026, he revealed... post-traumatic stress disorder due to episodes... since the surgery" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm revelation in March 2026 linked to surgery/lesion.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland won the 2026 Houston Open.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Current tournament leader, Gary Woodland... If Woodland were to hold on for the win in Houston" (leading into final round, implies win) (R1); "Gary Woodland... won... Texas Children's Houston Open" (R2); "Gary Woodland won the Houston Open" (R4); "Gary Woodland... victory at the Texas Children’s Houston Open" (R5); "won... Houston Open in 2026" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of 2026 win across sources.

verifications.claim: The 2026 Houston Open was Gary Woodland's first title since the surgery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first event since 2023 operation... first win since... 2019" (R2); "first victory since the U.S. Open" (2019, post-2023 surgery) (R4); "first win since the 2019 US Open" post-surgery (R5); "first professional victory since the 2019 U.S. Open" after surgery (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm it as first PGA Tour win since 2019 U.S. Open, after 2023 surgery.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland received the PGA Tour’s Courage Award in February 2025.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "named the recipient of the PGA Tour’s Courage Award... Woodland, 40, underwent brain surgery in Sept. 2023" (context implies post-surgery timing) (R3); "In February 2025, Woodland was awarded the PGA Tour Courage Award in recognition of his recovery from surgery" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: R8 directly states February 2025; R3 confirms award post-surgery.
